title: 2008 AMC 12B Problem 25
statement: Let \(ABCD\) be a trapezoid with \(AB \parallel CD,\) \(AB = 11,\) \(BC = 5,\) \(CD = 19,\) and \(DA = 7.\) Bisectors of \(\angle A\) and \(\angle D\) meet at \(P,\) and bisectors of \(\angle B\) and \(\angle C\) meet at \(Q.\) What is the area of hexagon \(ABQCDP?\)

solutions.text:
Because \(AB \parallel CD,\) \(\angle A + \angle D = 180^\circ,\) so the bisectors of \(\angle A\) and \(\angle D\) meet at right angles, \(\angle APD = 90^\circ.\) Then the midpoint \(M\) of \(\overline{AD}\) is the circumcenter of right triangle \(APD,\) giving \(MP = MA = MD.\) Thus \(\angle MPA = \angle PAM = \angle PAB,\) where the last equality uses the angle bisector at \(A.\) Therefore \(MP \parallel AB.\) The same argument gives \(QN \parallel AB\) for the midpoint \(N\) of \(\overline{BC}.\) Hence \(M, P, Q, N\) are collinear on the midline.

The midline has length \(\tfrac{AB + CD}{2} = 15,\) while \(MP = \tfrac{AD}{2} = \tfrac72\) and \(QN = \tfrac{BC}{2} = \tfrac52.\) Hence \(PQ = 15 - \tfrac72 - \tfrac52 = 9.\)

Drawing \(AE \parallel BC\) with \(E\) on \(\overline{CD}\) gives \(AE = 5\) and \(DE = CD - AB = 8.\) In \(\triangle ADE,\) \(\cos(\angle AED) = \tfrac{8^2 + 5^2 - 7^2}{2 \cdot 8 \cdot 5} = \tfrac12,\) so \(\angle AED = 60^\circ\) and the trapezoid’s height is \(AF = 5\sin 60^\circ = \tfrac{5\sqrt3}{2}.\)

The segment \(PQ\) sits at half the height, so the hexagon splits into two trapezoids and \[ \begin{aligned} &[ABQCDP] \\ &= \frac{AF}{4}\bigl(AB + CD + 2\,PQ\bigr) \\ &= \frac{\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}}{4}(11 + 19 + 18) \\ &= 30\sqrt3. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: \(\angle A + \angle D = 180^\circ,\) so their bisectors meet at right angles, and the midpoint of \(\overline{AD}\) is equidistant from \(A, D, P\)
This puts \(M, P, Q, N\) on the midline with \(PQ = \tfrac{AB + CD - AD - BC}{2};\) get the height from \(\triangle ADE\) (\(AE \parallel BC,\) sides \(7, 5, 8\))
